findings.title: Initial fixture preparation clones already immutable same-process owner events without a boundary need
findings.violatedProperty: The explicit user/Executive same-process identity rule requires retaining established immutable owner objects where no raw/process/byte admission or intentional cold reconstruction is selected.

evidence.fact: The new initial-prefix loop obtains an event from runtimeEventAtPrefixIndex and then runs JSON.stringify -> JSON.parse -> deepFreeze before pushing it into rows. Event ID strings and bytes may remain equal, but the event/payload objects acquire different references.
runtimeEventAtPrefixIndex returns the selected event object. The validated prefix already requires/establishes an immutable event snapshot and payloads; the owner reader is not a raw mutable ingress.

Each mode already owns a new rows array. Preparation appends retained/constructed events; later operations read/filter rows and append new frozen candidates. No mutation of a retained event body requires detaching it.
The later JSON roundtrip explicitly exercises cold reconstruction/projection equality. That existing byte-boundary witness is separate and should remain unchanged.

findings.causalAssessment: The author prepared the missing prefix by copying every event body although only a distinct container was needed. Deep immutability makes body references safe to share, and no caller mutation, process transfer, byte admission or negative-copy case is selected by the initial loop. There is no evidence-backed isolation need for the new copies.
findings.triggerProbability: Certain for each initial F04 prefix preparation on this frozen source.
findings.realizedHarm: Unnecessary serialization, cloning and identity loss in unshipped test setup; violation of the explicit construction constraint. No observed functional failure, shipped archive change or effect on the previously accepted archive performance measurement.
findings.blastRadius: Only F04 initial per-mode fixture setup and any local owner reuse dependent on those copied references. Native-workspace and the shared helper are unchanged by the needed correction; production consumers do not receive this test file.
findings.dependentPaths: Exact basis/projector preparation and subsequent component prefix reads consume the copied objects. The independent cold-replay comparison remains a deliberate copied-value path and is excluded from this finding.
findings.containment: All original functional tests pass; no Product code or archive member changed. The issue does not call for weakening guards or expanding Runtime scope.
findings.repairComplexity: Very small: retain the actual immutable event reference when adding it to the new fixture rows array. No new registry, schema logic, helper redesign or Product change is needed.
findings.regressionRisk: Low because retained events are immutable and the fixture mutates only its own container. Preserve the intentional cold-replay roundtrip and every original assertion.
findings.confidence: High on the identity violation and absence of a demonstrated boundary/isolation need. No numeric allocation/time impact was measured.
findings.workaroundOrContainment: Root may select the one-line setup correction; this Reviewer performs none.
findings.remainingProof: On a changed successor, source identity must be rebound and only the affected F04 whole-file proof needs renewal under Root selection. The exact unchanged native-workspace/helper proof can remain reusable through explicit correspondence; no broad rerun is implied.
